caveats: This is a supervised classification on the same samples used for DE in T1S2 — feature selection must be re-done inside each CV fold from the full feature matrix, not reuse T1S2's DE gene list, or the reported performance will be optimistically biased (established pitfall in high-dimensional expression classification, cf. Markowetz & Spang 2005 on nested-loop cross-validation and feature-selection bias)

60 vs 60 with ~12000 features is a high-dimensional, modest-n setting; report confidence intervals/variability across folds rather than a single point accuracy, and state plainly that internal CV performance is optimistic relative to a truly external, independently collected new sample
steps.question: Using the full filtered/normalized gene expression matrix (not the T1S2 DE gene list) as input, can a supervised classifier distinguish the 60 cases from 60 controls, and what is the honest cross-validated estimate of accuracy/AUC expected on a new, unseen sample?
acceptance_criteria: Classifier built with feature selection AND hyperparameter tuning performed strictly INSIDE each training fold of a nested cross-validation scheme (e.g. outer 5- or 10-fold CV for performance estimation, inner CV for feature selection/tuning) — the DE gene list from T1S2 is explicitly NOT used to pre-filter features for this step
At least two model families compared (e.g. elastic-net logistic regression via glmnet/sklearn, and a tree ensemble such as xgboost or random forest)

Report outer-fold AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and their mean +/- SD across outer folds as the unbiased performance estimate for a new sample; also report the naive (non-nested, feature-selection-outside-CV) estimate side by side to show the size of the optimism bias

Given n=60/60 (120 samples total, ~12000 features), the report explicitly states the number of samples per outer fold, discusses the instability/wide confidence intervals expected from a dataset this size relative to dimensionality, and does not claim generalizability beyond this cohort without external validation

Feature importance / selected-gene stability across outer folds reported (e.g. how often the same genes are selected) as an indicator of signal robustness rather than a claim of a fixed biomarker panel

steps.name: Synthesis: classifier feasibility and expected external accuracy
caveats: Single-batch cohort means no batch-effect cross-check is possible; any classifier signal could in principle reflect uncontrolled technical or demographic confounds not captured in the two-column metadata (condition only) — flag this explicitly given metadata.csv has only condition as a variable, i.e. no age/sex/batch covariates available to check for confounding
steps.question: Pulling together the DE signal, pathway/immune context, and nested-CV classifier performance, how well can a gene-expression classifier realistically be expected to distinguish case from control on a new sample from this cohort's data?
acceptance_criteria: Synthesizes T1S2 DE results, T2S1 pathway enrichment, T2S2 immune composition findings, and T3S1 nested-CV performance into a single accuracy statement with explicit uncertainty (CI or SD across folds)

States plainly whether the classifier signal appears biologically coherent (concordant with enriched pathways/immune shifts) or appears to be a weak/diffuse signal not clearly tied to interpretable biology

Explicitly separates internal cross-validated performance (this cohort) from expected performance on a genuinely external, independently collected sample, and states that only true external validation (a held-out or public replication cohort) can confirm generalizability — single-batch design here means batch effects are fully confounded with nothing to test against
No overclaiming: if nested-CV AUC is close to 0.5-0.6, states this directly as weak/insufficient for clinical use rather than framing it optimistically

plan.title: Whole-blood case vs control expression classifier
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq (Salmon gene-level counts, 12000 genes x 121 samples/120 metadata rows) from whole blood, 60 cases vs 60 controls, unpaired single-batch cohort. The research question asks two things: (1) can a gene-expression classifier separate cases from controls, and (2) what accuracy should be expected on a new sample. This requires: (a) rigorous QC/normalization of the count matrix and reconciliation of the 121 vs 120 sample count mismatch between counts and metadata, (b) a supervised differential-expression pass to characterize the case/control signal and provide biological interpretation (not as a feature-selection step feeding the classifier, to avoid leakage), (c) a classification step that performs feature selection and model fitting entirely inside cross-validation (nested CV) so the reported accuracy is not optimistically biased by prior DE-based gene selection on the full data, (d) pathway/immune-composition context for the DE genes to make the biology interpretable and to flag if the discriminative signal is simply driven by blood cell-type composition shifts (a common and important confound in whole-blood case/control designs), and (e) a synthesis of expected real-world performance including the honest caveat that n=60/60 whole blood is modest for a generalizable classifier and that a new external sample constitutes a much harder test than internal CV. Reference data used: WikiPathways human and MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets for enrichment (both present, human, matched organism); no curated blood-cell signature matrix (LM22 or equivalent) was found in the reference store, so immune deconvolution will rely on the immune-profiling agent's own built-in method rather than a store-provided reference, and that limitation is flagged in that step.
